the Fleckenstein EICA hypothesis, which was originally based on the observation of Ca(2+) overload in the myocardium of acute myocardial infarction patients and which was extended to include mitochondrial Ca(2+)-induced oxidative stress and mPTP opening, has been validated and remains a valid explanation for cardiomyocyte necrotic cell deaths in the heart.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

The main takeaway from our work is that
the Fleckenstein pathway is not a single event, but rather a series of events, each of which can be modified by a variety of therapeutic interventions.
the Fleckenstein concept, which has been largely ignored for the past 50 years, should be revisited and incorporated into the pathophysiological understanding of stressor-induced cardiomyocyte death.

EICA is a key factor which, when it occurs in the context of other factors that can compromise antioxidant defence and mitochondrial function, is a major determinant of cardiomyocyte loss in stressor-related heart diseases.
